WHEREAS the Government of Tamil Nadu is deeply committed to the conservation of Asiatic Elephants and need to notify elephant corridors, so as to ensure the unobstructed movement of Asian Elephants (Elephas maximus), long-term survival of the species and to mitigate human-Wildlife conflict;

8.2.1 Special Purpose Vehicle

“Chennai Rivers Transformation

Company Limited (CRTCL)” is a Special

Purpose Vehicle (SPV) established by the

Government of Tamil Nadu (GoTN) to implement

comprehensive river restoration and urban

regeneration initiatives for the waterways of

Chennai. The River basins of Chennai are linked

with the Cooum, Adyar, Kosasthalaiyar, Palar

basins and Buckingham Canal, supporting

irrigation, water supply and flood conveyance.

CRTCL aims to transform the city's river

systems into sustainable, climate-resilient and

socially inclusive urban assets.

8.2.2 Proposed Adyar and Cooum River restoration Projects The Government of Tamil Nadu led by the

vision of the Honorable Chief Minister will strive

with utmost resolve to restore the Cooum and the

Adyar rivers to their natural state. Rivers such as

the Cheonggyecheon in Seoul of South Korea and

the Kallang in Singapore have, through river

rejuvenation, become identities spoken of the

world over. On similar lines, Global tenders will be

invited and a Detailed Project Report will be

302

prepared to transform the Cooum and the Adyar

into the very identity of Chennai.

River Adyar, originates from Guduvancheri

(Chengalpattu District) and flows 43.4 km through

Tambaram, Thiruneermalai, Manapakkam,

Saidapet, Kotturpuram and Adyar before joining

the Bay of Bengal. Similarly, River Cooum

Originates from Cooum Tank (Tiruvallur), flows

65 km (including 20 km within Chennai) to the

Bay of Bengal.

The proposed Adyar and Cooum restoration

projects envisage an integrated river restoration

and urban transformation programme comprising,

inter alia:

 Interception, diversion and management of

wastewater entering the river.

 Water quality improvement measures.

 River ecosystem restoration and biodiversity

enhancement.

 Riverbank stabilization and environmental

improvements.

 Flood mitigation and climate resilience

interventions.

 Creation of public open spaces and riverfront

amenities.

 Urban landscape enhancement and public

realm development.

 Integration of sustainable mobility and

recreational infrastructure.

 Institutional strengthening and long-term

river management systems.

extracts.title: G.O.(Ms) No.150: Urban Development – Mandating the integration of infrastructure availability and hazard considerations into land use planning and zoning regulations – Orders – Issued.
extracts.text:
1.Preparation and enforcement of land use planning and zoning regulations incorporating infrastructure and

hazard restrictions.

It is proposed that formal land use planning and zoning regulations shall mandatorily incorporate critical parameters such as the availability of trunk infrastructure, including water supply, electricity, and sanitation systems, to ensure that development is aligned with service capabilities. Further, hazard mapping shall form an integral component of planning, identifying areas where development is prohibited due to natural hazards. In addition, hazard maps_ shall specify minimum separation between residential zones and hazardous occupancies. Accordingly, it is proposed to mandate the preparation and enforcement of land use plans and zoning regulations incorporating mandatory infrastructure requirements

and hazard-based restrictions.

2.Hazard maps shall be formally approved and published with prohibited zones, separation distances, no

construction areas

Further, hazard maps identifying prohibited zones, minimum separation distances, and no-construction areas shall be prepared, duly approved by the competent authority, and published for public access to ensure transparency and

awareness and implementation.

-3-

3.Establishing a regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on availability of trunk infrastructure

There is a need to establishing a regulatory framework that defines zoning parameters based on the availability and adequacy of trunk infrastructure. This framework shall ensure that development permissions are granted only where infrastructure systems are sufficient or planned to meet the projected demand, thereby preventing overburdening of services and ensuring orderly growth.

4. The above proposed measures are expected to result in a scientifically robust and legally enforceable planning system that promotes sustainable development, enhances public safety, protects natural resources, and ensures efficient utilization of infrastructure. It will also improve transparency, strengthen governance, and support informed decision-making.

5. In view of the above, the Commissioner of Town and Country Planning has requested the Government. issue necessary orders mandating the integration of infrastructure availability and hazard considerations into land use planning and zoning regulations, approving -and publishing hazard maps indicating prohibited zones, separation distances, and no-construction areas, and establishing a- regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on the availability of trunk infrastructure.

6. After careful consideration, the Government hereby, accept the request of Commissioner of Town and Country Planning and issue orders for mandating the integration of infrastructure availability and hazard considerations into land use planning and zoning regulations, approving and publishing hazard maps indicating prohibited zones, separation distances, and. no-construction areas, and establishing a regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on the availability of trunk infrastructure.

extracts.text:
1.Preparation and enforcement of land use planning and zoning regulations incorporating infrastructure and

hazard restrictions.

It is proposed that formal land use planning and zoning regulations shall mandatorily incorporate critical parameters such as the availability of trunk infrastructure, including water supply, electricity, and sanitation systems, to ensure that development is aligned with service capabilities. Further, hazard mapping shall form an integral component of planning, identifying areas where development is prohibited due to natural hazards. In addition, hazard maps_ shall specify minimum separation between residential zones and hazardous occupancies. Accordingly, it is proposed to mandate the preparation and enforcement of land use plans and zoning regulations incorporating mandatory infrastructure requirements

and hazard-based restrictions.

2.Hazard maps shall be formally approved and published with prohibited zones, separation distances, no

construction areas

Further, hazard maps identifying prohibited zones, minimum separation distances, and no-construction areas shall be prepared, duly approved by the competent authority, and published for public access to ensure transparency and

awareness and implementation.

-3-

3.Establishing a regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on availability of trunk infrastructure

There is a need to establishing a regulatory framework that defines zoning parameters based on the availability and adequacy of trunk infrastructure. This framework shall ensure that development permissions are granted only where infrastructure systems are sufficient or planned to meet the projected demand, thereby preventing overburdening of services and ensuring orderly growth.

4. The above proposed measures are expected to result in a scientifically robust and legally enforceable planning system that promotes sustainable development, enhances public safety, protects natural resources, and ensures efficient utilization of infrastructure. It will also improve transparency, strengthen governance, and support informed decision-making.

5. In view of the above, the Commissioner of Town and Country Planning has requested the Government. issue necessary orders mandating the integration of infrastructure availability and hazard considerations into land use planning and zoning regulations, approving -and publishing hazard maps indicating prohibited zones, separation distances, and no-construction areas, and establishing a- regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on the availability of trunk infrastructure.

6. After careful consideration, the Government hereby, accept the request of Commissioner of Town and Country Planning and issue orders for mandating the integration of infrastructure availability and hazard considerations into land use planning and zoning regulations, approving and publishing hazard maps indicating prohibited zones, separation distances, and. no-construction areas, and establishing a regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on the availability of trunk infrastructure.

rainfall. Twelve landslide hotspots identified

through scientific studies and field validation were

grouped into four clusters based on common

slope, terrain, geomorphological and land cover

characteristics. The proposal, with an estimated

119

outlay of Rs.50 crores, is currently under

consideration of the National Disaster

Management Authority (NDMA).

3.4.7.6 Scheme for the Mitigation of Coastal Erosion

Coastal Erosion poses a significant challenge

along several stretches of Tamil Nadu coastline.

A 32-year shoreline change analysis undertaken

by the National Centre for Coastal Research

(NCCR) for the period 1990–2022 found that 39

percent of the State's coastline is experiencing

varying degrees of erosion, with the highest

levels observed in Mayiladuthurai, Chengalpattu

and Kanyakumari districts. Based on these

findings, 15 socio-economically significant and

highly vulnerable hotspots along the coasts of

Tiruvallur, Chennai, Chengalpattu, Mayiladuthurai

120

and Kanyakumari have been identified for

intervention. The proposed project envisages

preparation and implementation of a Shoreline

Management Plan combining conventional

engineering measures with nature-based

solutions tailored to local conditions. The

proposal, with an estimated outlay of

Rs.225.15 crore, under consideration of

Government.

3.5.1 Landslide: Landslide Risk Mitigation Study

Heavy rainfall in Tamil Nadu’s hill districts

creates recurring landslide risks in the terrain

vulnerable to slope failure. To address this, the

Government engaged the Council for Energy,

Environment and Water (CEEW), New Delhi, to

121

undertake a scientific landslide risk assessment in

The Nilgiris, Valparai, Kodaikanal, Yercaud and

Yelagiri (G.O. (Ms) No. 72, Revenue and Disaster

Management Department, dated 13.02.2025).

The study will be extended to Tiruvannamalai

(Annamalayar Hills) with site-specific mitigation

measures to be developed based on its findings.

To mainstream disaster risk awareness

among youth, a comprehensive Disaster

Management curriculum has been developed by

a Syllabus Committee constituted by TNDRRA.

Based on the recommendations of the

Committee, the Tamil Nadu State Council for

Higher Education has advised all Universities to

122

introduce Disaster Management as a credit course

in undergraduate programmes across colleges in

the State.

5.2.3 Deficiency in capturing mandatory particulars

(i) Genuineness of educational qualification certificate of an employee joining Government service is ensured based on certificate obtained from Boards/Universities concerned. After recording the genuineness certificate details in SR, the employee is accorded ‘probationer’ status. IFHRMS did not have an input field to capture details of genuineness certificate received from Boards/Universities though SRS stipulated it.

An employee becomes eligible for ‘declaration of probation’ by HoO and for his second increment only on successful completion of compulsory training at Civil Service Training Institute, Bhavani Sagar followed by an assessment.

Audit observed that though employee training details can be captured along with attachments, none of the fields were mandatory2. Thus, ‘declaration of probation’ process could be completed even without capturing required information in the System.

Government replied (January 2023) that an input field to capture details of genuineness certificate would be provided and necessary provision to verify employee training details for declaration of probation would be explored.

5.2.4 No provision for HoOs to change employee status

SRS describes employee status as ‘Temporary’, ‘Probationer’ and ‘Approved Probationer’. Employee status had to be updated by HoO at every stage till employee attains ‘Approved Probationer’ status. Data analysis revealed that out of 9,76,122 active employees as of June 2022, 4,21,273 employees3 who joined service up to the year 20184 who would have completed probation were categorised as ‘Temporary’.

During the 18th Century, modern methods of silkworm rearing were introduced in Karnataka during the reign of the Mysore ruler, Tipu Sultan. During the latter half of the 20th century, modern sericulture was introduced into Tamil Nadu through Hosur and Thalavadi, the border areas adjoining Karnataka.

Subsequently, the impact of the Intensive Sericulture Development Programme, the introduction of high-yielding silkworm hybrids, their higher productivity and yield, and the assurance of stable income led to the spread of sericulture to other districts of the State.

2. Heritage of Tamil Nadu’s Silk Industry

Tamil Nadu has a long and rich tradition in the silk industry. There is evidence to show that silk has been in use in the State since the Sangam period. Renowned for its high-grade mulberry silk and exceptional craftsmanship, Tamil Nadu is one of the leading silk-producing States in India.

2

The Geographical Indication (GI)-tagged Kanchipuram silk sarees, Salem bivoltine silk dhotis, the intricate temple motif workmanship of Arani and Thirubuvanam silk sarees and the rich metallic thread (zari) workmanship of Sirumugai silk sarees, together proclaim to the world the timeless cultural glory of Tamil Nadu's silk weaving tradition.

The Department of Sericulture has been taking measures to sustain this legacy by ensuring a robust and continuous supply of raw materials. By embracing modern innovations while preserving tradition, sericulture continues to remain a sustainable livelihood activity.

3. Silk Production in the State

India is the only country in the world that produces all the four well-known varieties of silk, namely Mulberry, Eri, Tasar and Muga. Further, in India, mulberry silk is predominantly produced in the States of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, West Bengal, Maharashtra and Telangana.

3

Tamil Nadu is at the forefront in adopting the latest technologies in mulberry cultivation, silkworm rearing and silk reeling. Tamil Nadu ranks second at the national level in bivoltine silk production.

extracts.text:
a. Adoption of legally valid GIS-based Master, zonal, and land use plans.

To institutionalize and standardize these initiatives across all Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), Planning Authorities (UDA) it is proposed to mandate the preparation, approval, and adoption of GIS-based Master Plans, including Zonal Plans and Land Use Plans. All concerned authorities shall be required to follow standardized spatial and attribute structures, obtain statutory approval from the competent authority, and ensure formal adoption under relevant planning laws.

b. All ULBs/Authorities are directed to upload approved GIS based Plans for public access.

Further, all ULBs and UDAs shall be mandated to upload approved GIS-based plans on their official web portals and ensure public accessibility through user-friendly platforms.

c. Regulatory framework shall be established.

It is also proposed to establish a comprehensive regulatory framework defining the methodology, spatial standards and regulations of master plan preparation encompassing the processes such as baseline study with benchmarks, preparation of base map, preparation of existing land use map, existing situation analysis, identification of gaps and demands, stakeholders engagement, development proposals, preparation of proposed land use map, formulating the draft master plan and notifying final master plan using a standard operating procedure to ensure compliance and accountability.

Spatial Standards are as follows:

e Mapping Scale ~ Master Plan: 1:4,000; Zonal Plan: 1:2,000; Local Area Plan (LAP): 1:1,000; Site Plan: 1:500

e Horizontal Datum: World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS 84)

e Map Projection: Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM)

e Vertical Datum: WGS 84 Ellipsoidal Height, converted to Mean Sea Level (MSL) using an appropriate Geoid Model.

d. The spatial database shall include comprehensive GIS layers such as administrative boundaries, cadastral parcels (where available), transportation networks, existing and proposed land use, building footprints, water bodies, drainage, contours and terrain, utilities (water supply, sewerage, storm water, electricity, gas, telecommunications), environmental features, heritage assets, public and community facilities, green and open spaces, disasterprone areas, infrastructure corridors, and demographic and socioeconomic attributes linked through spatial identifiers.

e. The implementation of the above measures will result in a standardized, transparent, and legally robust planning system, enabling efficient urban development and improved governance. It will also strengthen public access to planning information and support data-driven decision-making.

4. In view of the above, the Commissioner of Town and Country Planning has requested the Government to issue necessary orders for mandating the preparation, approval, and adoption of legally valid GISbased Master Plans, Zonal Plans, and Land Use Plans, and directing all ULBs/Authorities to upload the approved GIS-based plans for public access, and for the establishment of a regulatory framework for standardized methodologies and GIS data layers.

3.Establishing a regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on availability of trunk infrastructure

There is a need to establishing a regulatory framework that defines zoning parameters based on the availability and adequacy of trunk infrastructure. This framework shall ensure that development permissions are granted only where infrastructure systems are sufficient or planned to meet the projected demand, thereby preventing overburdening of services and ensuring orderly growth.

4. The above proposed measures are expected to result in a scientifically robust and legally enforceable planning system that promotes sustainable development, enhances public safety, protects natural resources, and ensures efficient utilization of infrastructure. It will also improve transparency, strengthen governance, and support informed decision-making.

5. In view of the above, the Commissioner of Town and Country Planning has requested the Government. issue necessary orders mandating the integration of infrastructure availability and hazard considerations into land use planning and zoning regulations, approving -and publishing hazard maps indicating prohibited zones, separation distances, and no-construction areas, and establishing a- regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on the availability of trunk infrastructure.

6. After careful consideration, the Government hereby, accept the request of Commissioner of Town and Country Planning and issue orders for mandating the integration of infrastructure availability and hazard considerations into land use planning and zoning regulations, approving and publishing hazard maps indicating prohibited zones, separation distances, and. no-construction areas, and establishing a regulatory framework to define zoning parameters based on the availability of trunk infrastructure.
